reviews.title: Boring options
reviews.text:
My now husband and I have used this app for years. It’s basically became ritual, but as we’ve gotten older we have realized how boring this app is compared to our other relationship app. Firstly our preferred app is $6 a month with unlimited games, a home to decorate, plants to take care of, and animal to take care of, on top of a daily question, a sound track and mood tracker. ALL for $6 a month. 

The free version of this app gives you one singular question a day and you’re lucky if it’s not the same question asked 2 days ago just worded differently. 
I have had the prompt “share a photo of you S/O that makes you laugh”/ “share the goofiest photo of your s/o you have” /
“what’s the silliest photo of your s/o” 
this app feels like it has zero personality and zero chance to have personality. i’m very disappointed. 

we’ve been with this app for years hoping something will change or it would become more affordable, but $30 a month for an app in this economy especially is insane. 
can’t enjoy the paid version and i don’t think we’ll be enjoying the free version for much longer. 💔

reviews.title: Virtually impossible to use if you don’t pay for a subscription
reviews.text:
This app is super cute and fun to answer and discuss things with my girlfriend. We do our daily question, and it has really helped to spark ideas and deep conversations.

HOWEVER

If you want to be able to do anything besides a single question a day, you have to pay for it. You’d be better off just googling “couple conversation starters” and talking based on that. It’s just not worth it. Look elsewhere if you want a good app to consistently alter communication in your relationship.

reviews.title: They assign you woke pronouns
reviews.text:
We just got started with the app and like it so far. Lots of thoughtful activities and questions etc.  
Unfortunately we’re just a normal couple not from California and the app constantly uses they/them for my wife’s pronouns. Nowhere did she indicate anything that would make anyone assume she is a they/them.  
I’ve tried contacting support but all you get is a little AI chat bot that doesn’t understand anything. The support section also has a “report a bug“ tab but that just has this long article by Angela but no link to be able to just send something to support so they can look at it and fix it. 
It’s fine if people want to use whatever kind of pronouns but defaulting to the 0.001%  isn’t going to earn you a good review. 
The app has no way for the user to indicate pronouns and since they don’t they ought to go with the gender the user indicates in settings. 
$79 a year is a lot to pay for a buggy app with Bots for support. 
Beta releases are usually free and I accept bugs and glitches but for $79 it ought to work flawlessly. Someone should have thought of this.

reviews.title: Emotionally driven app
reviews.text: Pairs feels very one-sided. The app is heavily focused on emotions and communication in a way that seems to cater to one perspective, while overlooking how different people connect and build relationships. It often feels like one person’s feelings and needs take priority, and it doesn’t add much playfulness, fun, or lighthearted interaction to balance things out. Overall, it didn’t feel balanced or useful for our relationship.

reviews.title: Save your responses
reviews.text: I felt this app had valuable topics and introduced known researchers so found it great when trying to open up and get an “emotionally immature” partner to do the same. After months of thoughtful responses logged, my partner deleted the app in a “regular” pattern of showing me they can emotionally hurt and manipulate. I emailed and called Paired to restore my responses back to my account and they refuse to do so. Also, the developers created images of a heart shape for a scale. A response of “no” portrays an empty heart. Seems rather “heartless” for Paired to choose an empty heart when there are other shapes to share feedback with partners working to improve their relationship.

reviews.title: OK at first…
reviews.text:
It’s okay at first—then gets a little stale and repetitive. At first there was an option to shuffle the daily questions, then the developer eliminated that feature and made the app vastly less customizable. It’s probably best for couples in the first 5 - 10 years of marriage, but it doesn’t have tons of content and functionality for the 20+ year couples.

Still no update from the developers regarding ability to refresh or cycle through question / activity options. The app clearly is designed for folks in newer relationships…wish they had one for folks in very long-term relationships and in different stages of life (perimenopause, empty nesting, career transition, pre-retirement, “sandwich” generation, etc.).

reviews.title: Streak
reviews.text:
Dear Paired developers, 
This app has been a wonderful experience for me and my companion. I have gotten closer and connected in ways I could never think of on my own. The subscription has been affordable and the added benefits have been great. It hurts me to no end that additional transactions have made their way into a really great system. I lost over a two year streak due to my own forgetfulness and the circumstances of life, however, rather than being allowed to recover it by completing additional activities like I have in the past it is now expected that I pay a small fee instead. I thought this app has been a fantastic way to improve my relationship yet now it just feels like a cash grab trying to wiggle in additional charges wherever possible. I hope you get the money you are seeking, I hope it is worth it because you have lost a loyal fan and supporter. I will no longer recommend this app moving forward or invite others to use it. Best of luck. 
Sincerely,
Lava

reviews.title: Not built for us
reviews.text: We were excited to try this app. I envisioned an app that would be tailored to me, my relationship, and my preferences, and would be fun and useful in generating positive discussions. This has not been our experience. There is way too much content about sex and kink, which has made this uncomfortable for my spouse, and over emphasized the importance of this in our relationship. There are also a variety of relationship types man/woman, man/man, woman/woman that are repeatedly presented throughout the experience in terms of specific action plans and in simple visuals. I don’t have any issue with an app creator building something for a broad spectrum of potential clients, but once I’ve decided to try one that’s designed to benefit me and my specific relationship, I don’t want to be exposed to politically and socially sensitive topics of others sexuality. We attempted to use the app beyond the 7day trial period, not recognizing that these issues would make it unappealing to use until after we’d paid for an annual subscription. So we’ve got the app for a year but we’ve cancelled the renewal and have decided not to continue using it. Hope our experience will help you evaluate if you want to proceed past the 7day free trial.
